63.title: n²/2ⁿ: applying the AGP idea twice

board_content.text: Evaluate Σ n²/2ⁿ from n = 1 to ∞
Split $n^2 = n(n-1) + n$ to reuse two standard sums.
The AGP machinery, iterated, sums 'polynomial × geometric' series.

segments_english.text: We close the AGP examples with a sum that looks harder than an AGP but yields to the same idea applied twice. We want the sum of n squared over two to the n, to infinity.
The trick is a clean split: write n squared as n times n minus one, plus n. This turns one awkward sum into two sums we already have formulas for.
The two standard results are: the sum of n times n minus one times r to the n is two r squared over one minus r cubed, and the sum of n times r to the n is r over one minus r squared.
For the first piece with r equal one half, two times one quarter over one eighth gives four.
For the second piece, one half over one quarter gives two.
Adding the two pieces, four plus two is six. So the sum of n squared over two to the n is exactly six.
<excited> That is the real power of the AGP machinery — iterated, it sums any polynomial-times-geometric series. Split the polynomial into building blocks and apply the standard sums one at a time.

segments_hinglish.text: हम AGP examples को एक ऐसे sum से बंद करते हैं जो AGP से मुश्किल दिखता है पर उसी idea से हल हो जाता है, दो बार लगाकर। हमें n squared over two to the n का sum चाहिए, infinity तक।
trick एक clean split है: n squared को n times n minus one, plus n लिखो। यह एक awkward sum को दो sums में बदल देता है जिनके formulas हमारे पास पहले से हैं।
दो standard results हैं: n times n minus one times r to the n का sum है two r squared over one minus r cubed, और n times r to the n का sum है r over one minus r squared।
पहले piece के लिए r बराबर one half के साथ, two times one quarter over one eighth देता है four।
दूसरे piece के लिए, one half over one quarter देता है two।
दोनों pieces add करने पर, four plus two है six। तो n squared over two to the n का sum exactly six है।
<excited> यही AGP machinery की असली ताकत है — iterated, यह किसी भी polynomial-times-geometric series को sum कर देती है। polynomial को building blocks में split करो और standard sums एक-एक करके लगाओ।

64.title: AGP: the trap list and the pro-tips

board_content.text: AGP — the traps, and the fast moves
Wrong method: trying the AP or GP sum formula alone, or the Σ-polynomial method.
Convergence: write $S_\infty$ only after checking $|r| < 1$.
$r = 1$ means the AGP is a plain AP — use the AP sum, not division.
Don't swap which factor is the AP part and which is the GP part.
Pro-tip: re-derive $S_n$ with multiply-by-$r$ every time — faster than the formula.
For $S_\infty$, memorise the compact $\tfrac{a}{1-r} + \tfrac{d\,r}{(1-r)^2}$.
Recognise an AGP by shape: (linear in $n$) × ($r^{\,n-1}$).

segments_english.text: Let's gather the AGP traps and the fast moves that beat them.
The dominant error is reaching for the wrong tool — trying the AP sum formula alone, or the GP formula alone, or the polynomial-sum method. Each handles only one half of an AGP.
Second, respect convergence: write the sum-to-infinity formula only after confirming the size of r is below one — the same discipline as the plain GP.
Third, mind the degenerate case. When r equals one, the AGP is really just an AP, so sum it with the AP formula and never divide by one minus r.
Fourth, don't swap the roles — be clear which factor is the arithmetic part and which is the geometric part, because mixing up d and r derails the whole calculation.
<curious> Now the pro-tips. Don't memorise the messy finite sum — re-derive it with the multiply-by-r subtraction every time. It is faster and far more reliable under exam pressure.
For the infinite sum, do memorise the compact form: a over one minus r, plus d r over one minus r squared. That one is short enough to trust.
And above all, train the recognition: an AGP is anything shaped like something linear in n, multiplied by r to the n minus one. Spot that shape and you know instantly which method to swing.

segments_hinglish.text: चलो AGP traps और उन्हें हराने वाले fast moves इकट्ठा करें।
dominant error है गलत tool की तरफ़ पहुँचना — AP sum formula अकेले, या GP formula अकेले, या polynomial-sum method try करना। हर एक AGP का सिर्फ़ आधा हिस्सा handle करता है।
दूसरा, convergence का सम्मान करो: sum-to-infinity formula सिर्फ़ तब लिखो जब confirm कर लो कि r की size one से नीचे है — plain GP जैसा ही discipline।
तीसरा, degenerate case का ध्यान रखो। जब r equals one हो, तो AGP असल में बस एक AP है, तो इसे AP formula से sum करो और कभी one minus r से divide मत करो।
चौथा, roles मत बदलो — साफ़ रहो कि कौन सा factor arithmetic part है और कौन सा geometric, क्योंकि d और r को मिला देना पूरे calculation को पटरी से उतार देता है।
<curious> अब pro-tips। messy finite sum मत memorise करो — इसे हर बार multiply-by-r subtraction से re-derive करो। यह fast है और exam pressure में कहीं ज़्यादा reliable।
infinite sum के लिए, compact form ज़रूर memorise करो: a over one minus r, plus d r over one minus r squared। वो इतनी छोटी है कि भरोसा किया जा सके।
और सबसे ऊपर, recognition train करो: एक AGP कुछ भी है जो n में linear किसी चीज़ जैसा दिखे, r to the n minus one से गुणा। उस shape को spot करो और तुम्हें तुरंत पता है कौन सा method चलाना है।

segments_english.text: This unit is the computational engine of the chapter, and it rests on one move: break a complicated sum into simple sums you already know.

If you can write the general term as a combination of n cubed, n squared, n, and one, then by the linearity of the summation, the whole series is just the matching combination of the four standard sums.
The standard sums themselves come from a beautiful telescoping trick, shown on the board.

To find the sum of n squared, use the identity k cubed minus k minus one cubed equals three k squared minus three k plus one. Add it up for k from one to n and the left side collapses to just n cubed, leaving an equation you solve for the sum of squares.

<curious> And a point of real pride: the formulas for the sum of squares and the sum of cubes were first given by Aryabhata around four ninety-nine of the common era — over a thousand years before they appeared in European texts. When your students sum squares, they use an Indian result fifteen centuries old.
Here is a second intuition worth installing, also on the board: the sum of the first n cubes equals the square of the sum of the first n naturals.
So one plus eight plus twenty-seven is thirty-six, which is six squared, which is one plus two plus three, all squared. A startling, memorable coincidence.
The whole game is three steps: find the general term, express it in powers of n, and apply the standard sums.

तो one plus eight plus twenty-seven है thirty-six, जो six squared है, जो one plus two plus three, all squared है। एक चौंकाने वाला, याद रहने वाला coincidence।

66.title: The telescoping origin and the method of differences

board_content.text: Where the standard sums come from, and how to find $t_n$
Sum for $k = 1..n$: the left telescopes to $n^3$.
The same idea with $(k+1)^4 - k^4$ delivers $\sum n^3$.
Method of differences: if first differences form an AP, $t_n$ is quadratic.

segments_english.text: Let's see exactly where the standard sums come from, and then a technique for recovering an unknown general term.
The engine is the identity k cubed minus k minus one cubed equals three k squared minus three k plus one — a simple algebraic expansion.
Now sum both sides for k from one to n. On the left, everything cancels telescopically except the very last k cubed, so the left side is simply n cubed.

That gives n cubed equals three times the sum of k squared, minus three times the sum of k, plus n. Substituting the known sum of k and solving hands you the sum of squares: n times n plus one times two n plus one, over six.
The very same machinery, using k plus one to the fourth minus k to the fourth, delivers the sum of cubes.
And that sum of cubes is the tidy square: n times n plus one over two, all squared — one identity generating the whole family.

<curious> The second tool is the method of differences, for when you are handed terms but not a formula. If the first differences of the terms form an AP, then the general term is one degree higher — a quadratic.

For example, three, seven, thirteen, twenty-one have first differences four, six, eight, ten, an AP, so the general term is quadratic — solving gives n squared plus n plus one, after which the standard sums apply.

segments_hinglish.text: चलो देखें कि standard sums बिलकुल कहाँ से आते हैं, और फिर एक unknown general term को recover करने की technique।
engine है identity k cubed minus k minus one cubed equals three k squared minus three k plus one — एक simple algebraic expansion।
अब दोनों sides को k one से n तक sum करो। left पर, सब कुछ telescopically cancel हो जाता है सिवाय आख़िरी k cubed के, तो left side बस n cubed है।

इससे मिलता है n cubed equals three times sum of k squared, minus three times sum of k, plus n। known sum of k substitute करके solve करने पर sum of squares मिलता है: n times n plus one times two n plus one, over six।
वही machinery, k plus one to the fourth minus k to the fourth use करके, sum of cubes देती है।
और वो sum of cubes tidy square है: n times n plus one over two, all squared — एक identity पूरे family को generate करती है।
<curious> दूसरा tool है method of differences, तब के लिए जब तुम्हें terms दिए जाएँ पर formula नहीं। अगर terms के first differences एक AP बनाएँ, तो general term एक degree ऊँचा है — एक quadratic।

उदाहरण के लिए, three, seven, thirteen, twenty-one के first differences हैं four, six, eight, ten, एक AP, तो general term quadratic है — solve करने पर n squared plus n plus one मिलता है, जिसके बाद standard sums apply होते हैं।

67.title: The standard sums and the master technique

board_content.text: The four building-block sums, plus the master method

board_content.latex: t_n = an^3 + bn^2 + cn + d \;\Rightarrow\; S_n = a\!\sum n^3 + b\!\sum n^2 + c\!\sum n + dn

board_content.text: Products like $r(r+1)$ must be EXPANDED to a polynomial before summing.
Partial range: $\sum_m^n = \sum_1^n - \sum_1^{m-1}$.

segments_english.text: Let's consolidate the four building-block sums and the master technique that ties them together.
The two simplest: the sum of r is n times n plus one over two, and the sum of one is just n.
The sum of squares is n times n plus one times two n plus one, over six — commit this to memory carefully.
The sum of cubes is n times n plus one over two, all squared — the same numerator as the sum of r, but squared.
The sum of fourth powers is rarely needed and only for Advanced: n times n plus one times two n plus one times three n squared plus three n minus one, over thirty.
Now the master technique. If the general term is a cubic polynomial in n — a n cubed plus b n squared plus c n plus d — then the sum is the matching combination of the standard sums, term by term.

<whisper> Here is the condition students forget: the technique only works when the general term is a polynomial. So a product like r times r plus one must be expanded into a polynomial first — never sum it as a product.
And for a sum that does not start at one, use the partial-range trick: the sum from m to n equals the sum up to n minus the sum up to m minus one.

segments_hinglish.text: चलो चार building-block sums और उन्हें जोड़ने वाली master technique consolidate करें।
दो सबसे simple: sum of r है n times n plus one over two, और sum of one बस n है।
sum of squares है n times n plus one times two n plus one, over six — इसे ध्यान से memory में डालो।
sum of cubes है n times n plus one over two, all squared — sum of r जैसा ही numerator, पर squared।
sum of fourth powers शायद ही कभी चाहिए और सिर्फ़ Advanced के लिए: n times n plus one times two n plus one times three n squared plus three n minus one, over thirty।
अब master technique। अगर general term n में एक cubic polynomial हो — a n cubed plus b n squared plus c n plus d — तो sum standard sums का matching combination है, term by term।

<whisper> यह रही वो condition जो students भूल जाते हैं: technique सिर्फ़ तब काम करती है जब general term एक polynomial हो। तो r times r plus one जैसे product को पहले polynomial में expand करना होगा — इसे कभी product की तरह sum मत करो।
और एक ऐसे sum के लिए जो one से शुरू नहीं होता, partial-range trick use करो: m से n तक sum equals sum up to n minus sum up to m minus one।

board_content.text: Find the sum to n terms of 2·4 + 4·6 + 6·8 + …
Factor out $2n(n+1)$ and combine the bracket.
Expand the product to a polynomial FIRST — then the standard sums apply.

segments_english.text: Let's start the special-series examples with a product series. We want the sum to n terms of two times four, plus four times six, plus six times eight, and so on.
First find the general term. The r-th term is two r times two r plus two, which expands to four r squared plus four r — a clean polynomial.
Now apply linearity: the sum is four times the sum of r squared, plus four times the sum of r.
Substitute the standard sums: four times n times n plus one times two n plus one over six, plus four times n times n plus one over two.
Factor out the common two n times n plus one and combine what's left inside the bracket.
The whole thing tidies beautifully to four n times n plus one times n plus two, over three.

<curious> The one habit to internalise: expand the product into a polynomial first. Never try to sum a product like two r times two r plus two directly — the standard sums only apply once it is in powers of n.

segments_hinglish.text: चलो special-series examples एक product series से शुरू करें। हमें two times four, plus four times six, plus six times eight का n terms तक sum चाहिए, और ऐसे ही।
पहले general term निकालो। r-th term है two r times two r plus two, जो expand होकर four r squared plus four r बनता है — एक clean polynomial।
अब linearity apply करो: sum है four times sum of r squared, plus four times sum of r।
standard sums substitute करो: four times n times n plus one times two n plus one over six, plus four times n times n plus one over two।
common two n times n plus one बाहर निकालो और bracket के अंदर बचे हुए को combine करो।
पूरी चीज़ खूबसूरती से four n times n plus one times n plus two, over three में सिमट जाती है।

<curious> internalise करने लायक एक habit: product को पहले polynomial में expand करो। two r times two r plus two जैसे product को कभी सीधे sum मत करो — standard sums तभी apply होते हैं जब यह n की powers में हो।

board_content.text: First differences 4, 6, 8, 10 form an AP ⇒ $t_n$ is quadratic.

segments_english.text: This example needs the method of differences, because we're given the terms with no formula in sight. The series is three, seven, thirteen, twenty-one, thirty-one.
Take the first differences: four, six, eight, ten. Those form an arithmetic progression, which is the signal that the general term is quadratic in n.
Fitting a quadratic to the first few terms gives the general term n squared plus n plus one. Check the fourth term: sixteen plus four plus one is twenty-one, which matches.
Now sum term by term using linearity: the sum of n squared, plus the sum of n, plus the sum of one.
Substitute the standard formulas: n times n plus one times two n plus one over six, plus n times n plus one over two, plus n.
Combining over a common factor, everything collapses to n times n squared plus three n plus five, over three.

<curious> And always verify with a small case. The sum of the first three terms should be three plus seven plus thirteen, which is twenty-three — and the formula gives three times nine plus nine plus five over three, also twenty-three. It checks.

segments_hinglish.text: इस example को method of differences चाहिए, क्योंकि हमें terms दिए गए हैं बिना कोई formula दिखे। series है three, seven, thirteen, twenty-one, thirty-one।
first differences लो: four, six, eight, ten। ये एक arithmetic progression बनाते हैं, जो संकेत है कि general term n में quadratic है।
पहले कुछ terms पर एक quadratic fit करने से general term n squared plus n plus one मिलता है। fourth term check करो: sixteen plus four plus one है twenty-one, जो match करता है।
अब linearity use करके term by term sum करो: sum of n squared, plus sum of n, plus sum of one।
standard formulas substitute करो: n times n plus one times two n plus one over six, plus n times n plus one over two, plus n।
common factor पर combine करने पर, सब कुछ n times n squared plus three n plus five, over three में सिमट जाता है।

<curious> और हमेशा एक small case से verify करो। पहले तीन terms का sum three plus seven plus thirteen होना चाहिए, यानी twenty-three — और formula देता है three times nine plus nine plus five over three, भी twenty-three। यह check हो गया।

70.title: A nested sum of triangular numbers

board_content.text: Evaluate Σ (1 + 2 + 3 + … + k) for k = 1 to 20
The inner sum is the triangular number $\tfrac{k(k+1)}{2}$.
JEE Main 2020: resolve the inner sum first, then apply standard sums.

segments_english.text: This is a JEE Main problem that hides a sum inside a sum. We must evaluate the sum, for k from one to twenty, of the quantity one plus two plus three up to k.
The inner sum is a familiar object — the triangular number, k times k plus one over two. So substitute that in place of the inner expression.
The outer sum then becomes one half times the sum of k squared plus the sum of k, both taken from one to twenty.
Compute the sum of squares up to twenty: twenty times twenty-one times forty-one over six, which is two thousand eight hundred seventy.
Compute the sum of the naturals up to twenty: twenty times twenty-one over two, which is two hundred ten.
Adding those and halving: one half of two thousand eight hundred seventy plus two hundred ten is one thousand five hundred forty.

<curious> The lesson from this JEE Main favourite is to resolve the inner sum first — turn it into a clean polynomial in k — and only then bring in the standard sums. Nested sums are just two ordinary sums, one inside the other.

segments_hinglish.text: यह एक JEE Main problem है जो एक sum के अंदर एक sum छुपाता है। हमें k one से twenty तक, quantity one plus two plus three up to k का sum evaluate करना है।
inner sum एक familiar object है — triangular number, k times k plus one over two। तो इसे inner expression की जगह substitute करो।
outer sum तब बन जाता है one half times sum of k squared plus sum of k, दोनों one से twenty तक।
twenty तक sum of squares compute करो: twenty times twenty-one times forty-one over six, यानी two thousand eight hundred seventy।
twenty तक naturals का sum compute करो: twenty times twenty-one over two, यानी two hundred ten।
इन्हें add करके half करो: one half of two thousand eight hundred seventy plus two hundred ten है one thousand five hundred forty।
<curious> इस JEE Main favourite का सबक है inner sum को पहले resolve करना — इसे k में एक clean polynomial में बदलो — और तभी standard sums लाओ। nested sums बस दो ordinary sums हैं, एक दूसरे के अंदर।

board_content.text: Find $S_n$ for 5 + 55 + 555 + …
Each term is 5 times a repunit: $t_r = 5\cdot\frac{10^r - 1}{9}$.
Peel off the GP piece $10^r$ and the constant $-1$ separately.
A GP-based special series — geometric part summed, constant part is $-n$.

segments_english.text: This example handles a series whose terms are made of repeated digits. We want the sum of five plus fifty-five plus five hundred fifty-five, and so on.
The key trick is rewriting each term. A repunit — a string of ones — equals ten to the r minus one, over nine. So the r-th term is five times ten to the r minus one, over nine.
Pull the constant five ninths outside, and the sum becomes five ninths times the sum of ten to the r minus one, for r from one to n.
Split that inside: the ten-to-the-r piece is a geometric progression summing to ten times ten to the n minus one over nine, and the minus one piece contributes a simple minus n.
Putting it together and simplifying, the sum is five over eighty-one times the quantity ten to the n plus one, minus nine n, minus ten.
<curious> The strategy generalises: when a series is built from repeated digits, peel off the geometric piece ten to the r and the constant separately, sum each on its own, and recombine.
So this is a geometric-based special series — the geometric part is summed with the GP formula, and the constant part simply contributes minus n.

segments_hinglish.text: यह example एक ऐसी series handle करता है जिसके terms repeated digits से बने हैं। हमें five plus fifty-five plus five hundred fifty-five का sum चाहिए, और ऐसे ही।
key trick है हर term को फिर से लिखना। एक repunit — ones की एक string — equals ten to the r minus one, over nine। तो r-th term है five times ten to the r minus one, over nine।
constant five ninths बाहर खींचो, और sum बन जाता है five ninths times sum of ten to the r minus one, r one से n तक।
उसके अंदर split करो: ten-to-the-r piece एक geometric progression है जो sum होकर ten times ten to the n minus one over nine बनता है, और minus one piece एक simple minus n contribute करता है।
इसे जोड़कर और simplify करके, sum है five over eighty-one times the quantity ten to the n plus one, minus nine n, minus ten।

तो यह एक geometric-based special series है — geometric part GP formula से sum होता है, और constant part बस minus n contribute करता है।

72.title: Sum of squares of an AP's terms

board_content.text: If $S_n = cn^2$ for an AP, find the sum of the squares of its terms
$S_n = cn^2$ is $An^2 + Bn$ with $B = 0$, so it's an AP.
Recover $a_n$ from $S_n$ via $a_n = S_n - S_{n-1}$, then square and sum.

segments_english.text: This JEE Advanced problem links the sum-characterization back to special series. We're told the sum of the first n terms of an AP is c times n squared, and asked for the sum of the squares of those terms.
First, recognise the structure. c n squared is of the form A n squared plus B n with B zero, so this genuinely is an AP.
Recover the general term using the sum difference: a sub n equals S sub n minus S sub n minus one, which is c times n squared minus n minus one squared, giving c times two n minus one.
Now sum the squares: c squared times the sum of two n minus one squared, which expands to c squared times the sum of four n squared minus four n plus one.
Substitute the standard sums: four times the sum of squares, minus four times the sum of n, plus the sum of one, all scaled by c squared.
Simplifying the bracket, everything collapses to N times four N squared minus one, times c squared, over three.

<curious> The reusable move here is the recovery step — whenever you're given the sum but need the terms, take the difference of consecutive sums, and then the special-series machinery finishes the job.

segments_hinglish.text: यह JEE Advanced problem sum-characterization को वापस special series से जोड़ता है। हमें बताया गया है कि एक AP के पहले n terms का sum c times n squared है, और उन terms के squares का sum पूछा गया है।
पहले, structure पहचानो। c n squared, A n squared plus B n के form का है जिसमें B zero है, तो यह सच में एक AP है।
sum difference use करके general term recover करो: a sub n equals S sub n minus S sub n minus one, यानी c times n squared minus n minus one squared, देता है c times two n minus one।
अब squares sum करो: c squared times sum of two n minus one squared, जो expand होकर c squared times sum of four n squared minus four n plus one बनता है।
standard sums substitute करो: four times sum of squares, minus four times sum of n, plus sum of one, सब c squared से scaled।
bracket simplify करने पर, सब कुछ N times four N squared minus one, times c squared, over three में सिमट जाता है।
<curious> यहाँ reusable move recovery step है — जब भी तुम्हें sum दिया जाए पर terms चाहिए, consecutive sums का difference लो, और फिर special-series machinery काम पूरा कर देती है।

73.title: Cubes over odd sums collapse to a quadratic

board_content.text: Numerator is $\sum r^3 = \left[\tfrac{r(r+1)}{2}\right]^2$; denominator is $1+3+\cdots+(2r-1) = r^2$.
Both standard sums collapse the term to a clean quadratic before summing.

segments_english.text: We finish with an Advanced series where two standard sums appear inside a single term. The r-th term is the sum of cubes up to r, divided by the sum of odd numbers up to the r-th odd.
Simplify the two pieces. The numerator is the sum of cubes, which is r times r plus one over two, all squared. The denominator, one plus three up to two r minus one, is exactly r squared.
Dividing, the r squared cancels beautifully and the whole term collapses to r plus one, squared, over four — a clean quadratic.
So the sum is one quarter times the sum of r plus one squared, which we expand as one quarter times the sum of r squared plus two r plus one.
Substitute the standard sums: n times n plus one times two n plus one over six, plus n times n plus one, plus n, all scaled by one quarter.
Simplifying, the result is n times two n squared plus nine n plus thirteen, over twenty-four.

<excited> This is the signature special-series move — two known sums, one in the numerator and one in the denominator, collapse the ugly-looking term into a tidy quadratic, and from there the standard sums finish everything.

segments_hinglish.text: हम एक Advanced series से खत्म करते हैं जहाँ एक ही term के अंदर दो standard sums आते हैं। r-th term है r तक cubes का sum, divided by r-th odd तक odd numbers का sum।
दोनों pieces simplify करो। numerator है sum of cubes, यानी r times r plus one over two, all squared। denominator, one plus three से two r minus one तक, exactly r squared है।
divide करने पर, r squared खूबसूरती से cancel हो जाता है और पूरा term r plus one, squared, over four में सिमट जाता है — एक clean quadratic।
तो sum है one quarter times sum of r plus one squared, जिसे हम one quarter times sum of r squared plus two r plus one के रूप में expand करते हैं।
standard sums substitute करो: n times n plus one times two n plus one over six, plus n times n plus one, plus n, सब one quarter से scaled।
simplify करने पर, result है n times two n squared plus nine n plus thirteen, over twenty-four।

<excited> यह signature special-series move है — दो known sums, एक numerator में और एक denominator में, ugly दिखने वाले term को एक tidy quadratic में collapse कर देते हैं, और वहाँ से standard sums सब कुछ खत्म कर देते हैं।

74.title: Special Series: the traps and the pro-tips

board_content.text: Special series — the traps, and the fast moves
Formula confusion: swapping $\sum n^2$ (the $/6$ form) and $\sum n^3$ (the squared form).
Term recognition: find $t_n$ as a polynomial BEFORE summing (expand products).
Index range: use $\sum_1^n - \sum_1^{m-1}$ when a sum doesn't start at 1.
Method of differences: don't mis-degree $t_n$ by checking only first differences.
Pro-tip: find $t_n$ → expand to powers of $n$ → apply standard sums.
Shortcut: $\sum n^3 = (\sum n)^2$ — recognise cubes on sight.
Forgot $\sum n^2$? Re-derive in 4 lines from $k^3 - (k-1)^3$.

segments_english.text: Let's gather the special-series traps and the moves that beat them.

The dominant error is formula confusion — swapping the sum of squares, with its over-six form, and the sum of cubes, which is a squared expression. Keep the three standard sums cleanly separated in memory.
Second is term recognition: you must find the general term as a polynomial before summing. A product like r times r plus one has to be expanded first — never summed as a product.
Third, watch the index range. When a sum doesn't start at one, use the partial-range correction: the sum up to n minus the sum up to m minus one.
Fourth, in the method of differences, don't mis-degree the term. Checking only the first differences when you should check the second is a common way to treat a quadratic as if it were linear.
<curious> The pro-tip is a single workflow that solves most problems: find the general term, expand it into powers of n, then apply the standard sums. Drill that sequence until it's automatic.
Keep the fastest shortcut ready: the sum of cubes equals the square of the sum. Recognise cubes on sight and you skip a whole computation.
And if you ever blank on the sum of squares, don't panic — re-derive it in four lines from the identity k cubed minus k minus one cubed. The telescoping origin is your safety net.

segments_hinglish.text: चलो special-series traps और उन्हें हराने वाले moves इकट्ठा करें।
dominant error है formula confusion — sum of squares, अपने over-six form के साथ, और sum of cubes, जो एक squared expression है, को आपस में swap करना। तीनों standard sums को memory में साफ़ अलग रखो।
दूसरा है term recognition: तुम्हें sum करने से पहले general term को एक polynomial के रूप में निकालना होगा। r times r plus one जैसे product को पहले expand करना होगा — कभी product की तरह sum मत करो।
तीसरा, index range देखो। जब sum one से शुरू न हो, partial-range correction use करो: sum up to n minus sum up to m minus one।
चौथा, method of differences में, term को mis-degree मत करो। जब second differences check करने चाहिए तब सिर्फ़ first differences check करना एक common तरीका है quadratic को linear मान लेने का।

<curious> pro-tip एक single workflow है जो ज़्यादातर problems solve करता है: general term निकालो, इसे n की powers में expand करो, फिर standard sums apply करो। इस sequence को तब तक drill करो जब तक यह automatic न हो जाए।
सबसे fast shortcut तैयार रखो: sum of cubes equals square of the sum। cubes को देखते ही पहचानो और तुम एक पूरा computation छोड़ देते हो।
और अगर तुम कभी sum of squares पर blank हो जाओ, तो घबराओ मत — इसे identity k cubed minus k minus one cubed से चार line में re-derive करो। telescoping origin तुम्हारा safety net है।

board_content.text: Like a relay: only the starting baton and the finish-line position matter.

segments_english.text: This final unit handles the sums that Unit seven cannot touch — where the general term is not a polynomial. The core idea is telescoping.
The picture says it all. A telescoping sum works like a collapsing telescope: each term cancels part of the next, so when you add everything, only the very first and very last pieces survive.
Formally, if you can write the r-th term as V-r minus V-r-plus-one, then the whole sum from one to n collapses to just V-one minus V-n-plus-one.
Think of a relay race where each runner hands off exactly what they received. Only the starting baton and the finish-line position matter; everything passed in between cancels in the bookkeeping.
The question is how to force a term into that difference-form. For a fraction, the tool is partial fractions.
For instance, one over r times r plus one splits cleanly into one over r minus one over r plus one — a perfect consecutive difference.
For products of consecutive integers, the tool is the V-n method — append a factor and divide. And for a surd in the denominator, you rationalise, which almost always produces a telescoper.
<curious> Keep the big picture: this unit is precisely the tool for non-polynomial general terms, exactly where Unit seven's standard-sum formulas break down.

segments_hinglish.text: यह आख़िरी unit उन sums को handle करता है जिन्हें Unit seven छू भी नहीं सकता — जहाँ general term एक polynomial नहीं है। core idea है telescoping।
picture सब कह देती है। एक telescoping sum एक collapsing telescope की तरह काम करती है: हर term अगले का हिस्सा cancel कर देता है, तो जब तुम सब कुछ add करते हो, सिर्फ़ पहला और आख़िरी piece बचता है।

सवाल है कि एक term को उस difference-form में कैसे force करें। एक fraction के लिए, tool है partial fractions।
उदाहरण के लिए, one over r times r plus one साफ़ split होता है one over r minus one over r plus one में — एक perfect consecutive difference।

<curious> big picture रखो: यह unit ठीक उन non-polynomial general terms का tool है, exactly वहाँ जहाँ Unit seven के standard-sum formulas टूट जाते हैं।

board_content.text: Partial fractions, the $V_n$ method, factorials, and surds
$V_n$ method: with $V_r = r(r+1)(r+2)$, we get $V_r - V_{r-1} = 3\,r(r+1)$.
Every derivation is the same shape: force a difference, then only ends survive.

segments_english.text: Let's build the standard telescopers, and notice they all share one shape.
First, the workhorse. One over r times r plus one splits into one over r minus one over r plus one, and summing collapses to one minus one over n plus one, which is n over n plus one.

For the triple product, one over r times r plus one times r plus two, split it as one half times the difference of one over r times r plus one and one over r plus one times r plus two. The bracket telescopes.
Now the V-n method for a product. Take V-r as r times r plus one times r plus two. Then V-r minus V-r-minus-one works out to three times r times r plus one.
So r times r plus one is one third of that difference, and the sum telescopes to one third of n times n plus one times n plus two.
For factorials, notice r times r-factorial equals r-plus-one-factorial minus r-factorial. Summing that telescopes cleanly to n-plus-one-factorial minus one.
And for surds, rationalising one over root r plus root r plus one gives root r plus one minus root r — a difference ready to collapse to root n plus one minus one.
<curious> Feel the common thread: every single derivation is the same move — force the term into a difference of consecutive things, and then only the endpoints survive.

segments_hinglish.text: चलो standard telescopers बनाएँ, और ध्यान दो कि ये सब एक ही shape share करते हैं।
पहले, workhorse। one over r times r plus one, one over r minus one over r plus one में split होता है, और sum करने पर one minus one over n plus one में collapse होता है, यानी n over n plus one।

अब एक product के लिए V-n method। V-r को r times r plus one times r plus two लो। तब V-r minus V-r-minus-one निकलता है three times r times r plus one।
तो r times r plus one उस difference का one third है, और sum telescope होकर one third of n times n plus one times n plus two बनता है।

और surds के लिए, one over root r plus root r plus one को rationalise करने पर root r plus one minus root r मिलता है — एक difference जो root n plus one minus one में collapse होने को तैयार है।

board_content.text: The principle and the standard results

board_content.text: Track the constant multiplier ($\tfrac12$, $\tfrac1k$) — dropping it is a classic slip.

segments_english.text: Let's consolidate the telescoping toolkit — the principle first, then the standard results worth recognising on sight.
The principle is the whole unit in one line: if the r-th term is V-r minus V-r-plus-one, the sum is simply V-one minus V-n-plus-one.
The first standard result: the sum of one over r times r plus one is n over n plus one.
The triple-product sum is n times n plus three, over four times n plus one times n plus two.
For the odd-factor product, the sum of one over two r minus one times two r plus one is n over two n plus one.
The V-n method generalises the whole family: the sum of a product of k consecutive integers is the product of k plus one consecutive integers, divided by k plus one.
And two more to keep close: the sum of r times r-factorial is n-plus-one-factorial minus one, and the surd sum is root n plus one minus one.

<whisper> One warning that catches people out: track the constant multiplier. The triple product carries a one half, the odd-factor split carries a one half too — dropping that constant is a classic, silent slip.

principle पूरा unit एक line में है: अगर r-th term V-r minus V-r-plus-one हो, तो sum बस V-one minus V-n-plus-one है।
पहला standard result: one over r times r plus one का sum है n over n plus one।
triple-product sum है n times n plus three, over four times n plus one times n plus two।
odd-factor product के लिए, one over two r minus one times two r plus one का sum है n over two n plus one।
V-n method पूरे family को generalise करता है: k consecutive integers के product का sum, k plus one consecutive integers का product है, k plus one से divided।
और दो और पास रखो: r times r-factorial का sum है n-plus-one-factorial minus one, और surd sum है root n plus one minus one।
<whisper> एक warning जो लोगों को पकड़ती है: constant multiplier track करो। triple product एक one half रखता है, odd-factor split भी एक one half — उस constant को गिरा देना एक classic, silent slip है।

78.title: The basic telescoper and its infinite limit

board_content.text: Find Σ 1/[r(r+1)] to n terms, and its value as n → ∞
Every interior term appears once with $+$ and once with $-$.

segments_english.text: Let's open the telescoping examples with the cleanest case — the sum of one over r times r plus one, and what it approaches as n grows.
The first move is partial fractions: one over r times r plus one splits into one over r minus one over r plus one.
Now write out the sum term by term: one minus one half, plus one half minus one third, and so on to one over n minus one over n plus one.
Look at what happens. Every interior fraction appears once with a plus and once with a minus, so they annihilate in pairs.
Only the outermost survivors remain: the leading one, and the trailing minus one over n plus one. So the sum is one minus one over n plus one, which is n over n plus one.
As n grows without bound, that trailing fraction vanishes and the sum approaches one.
<excited> So the infinite series one over one-times-two, plus one over two-times-three, and onward, equals exactly one — a beautifully clean result straight out of the collapse.

segments_hinglish.text: चलो telescoping examples को सबसे clean case से खोलें — one over r times r plus one का sum, और यह n बढ़ने पर किसकी तरफ़ जाता है।
पहला move है partial fractions: one over r times r plus one, one over r minus one over r plus one में split होता है।
अब sum को term by term लिखो: one minus one half, plus one half minus one third, और ऐसे ही one over n minus one over n plus one तक।
देखो क्या होता है। हर interior fraction एक बार plus के साथ और एक बार minus के साथ आता है, तो वे pairs में एक-दूसरे को खत्म कर देते हैं।
सिर्फ़ बाहरी survivors बचते हैं: शुरू का one, और आख़िरी minus one over n plus one। तो sum है one minus one over n plus one, यानी n over n plus one।
जैसे-जैसे n बिना सीमा बढ़ता है, वो आख़िरी fraction गायब हो जाता है और sum one की तरफ़ पहुँचता है।
<excited> तो infinite series one over one-times-two, plus one over two-times-three, और आगे, exactly one के बराबर है — collapse से सीधे निकला एक खूबसूरत clean result।

79.title: A partial-fraction telescoper with a step of 3

board_content.text: The factors step by 3: general term is $\tfrac{1}{(3r-2)(3r+1)}$.
The bracket telescopes; the $\tfrac13$ rides along outside.
Keep the $\tfrac13$ from the split — losing it is the telescope-lost-multiplier trap.

segments_english.text: This example is the same idea with a twist — the denominators step by three instead of one, and a constant multiplier appears.
Read the pattern in the denominators: one and four, four and seven, seven and ten. So the r-th term is one over three r minus two, times three r plus one.
Partial fractions split this, but watch the constant: it becomes one third times the difference of one over three r minus two and one over three r plus one.
The bracket telescopes exactly as before, while the one third simply rides along on the outside of the whole sum.
After the interior terms cancel, we're left with one third times the quantity one minus one over three n plus one.
Simplifying, that is n over three n plus one.

<whisper> The one thing to guard here is that factor of one third from the split. Forgetting it gives a plausible-looking answer that's wrong by a factor of three — the telescope-lost-multiplier trap.

segments_hinglish.text: यह example वही idea है एक twist के साथ — denominators one के बजाय three से step करते हैं, और एक constant multiplier आता है।
denominators में pattern पढ़ो: one और four, four और seven, seven और ten। तो r-th term है one over three r minus two, times three r plus one।
partial fractions इसे split करते हैं, पर constant देखो: यह बनता है one third times the difference of one over three r minus two और one over three r plus one।

interior terms cancel होने के बाद, हमारे पास बचता है one third times the quantity one minus one over three n plus one।
simplify करने पर, यह है n over three n plus one।
<whisper> यहाँ guard करने वाली एक चीज़ है split से आया वो one third factor। इसे भूलना एक plausible दिखने वाला answer देता है जो three के factor से गलत है — telescope-lost-multiplier trap।

80.title: The Vₙ method on a product of three

board_content.text: Find Σ r(r+1)(r+2) from r = 1 to n
A product of 3 consecutive integers — use the $V_n$ method.
Here $k = 3$: append one more factor, divide by $k + 1 = 4$.
Divide by (number of factors + 1) — the $V_n$-method-divisor rule.

segments_english.text: This example shows the V-n method at its cleanest, on a product of three consecutive integers.
Rather than expand into a cubic and sum term by term, we use the V-n shortcut, which mirrors how integration raises a power.
The general rule: the sum of a product of k consecutive integers equals the product of k plus one consecutive integers, divided by k plus one.
Here k is three. So we append one more factor — n plus three — and divide by k plus one, which is four.
That gives the sum directly as n times n plus one times n plus two times n plus three, over four.
Verify with n equals one: the sum should be one times two times three, which is six, and the formula gives one times two times three times four over four, also six. It checks.
<curious> The one rule to lock in is the divisor: you divide by the number of factors plus one. Using the wrong divisor is the classic V-n-method slip.

segments_hinglish.text: यह example V-n method को उसके सबसे clean रूप में दिखाता है, तीन consecutive integers के एक product पर।
एक cubic में expand करके term by term sum करने के बजाय, हम V-n shortcut use करते हैं, जो mirror करता है कि integration एक power कैसे बढ़ाता है।
general rule: k consecutive integers के product का sum, k plus one consecutive integers के product के बराबर है, k plus one से divided।
यहाँ k three है। तो हम एक और factor append करते हैं — n plus three — और k plus one, यानी four से divide करते हैं।
इससे sum सीधे मिलता है n times n plus one times n plus two times n plus three, over four।
n equals one से verify करो: sum one times two times three, यानी six होना चाहिए, और formula देता है one times two times three times four over four, भी six। यह check हो गया।
<curious> lock करने वाला एक rule है divisor: तुम number of factors plus one से divide करते हो। गलत divisor use करना classic V-n-method slip है।

board_content.text: Evaluate Σ r/(r+1)! from r = 1 to n
Rewrite the numerator: $r = (r+1) - 1$.
This is a difference of consecutive reciprocal factorials.
Look for $t_r = f(r) - f(r+1)$ with $f$ a factorial expression.

segments_english.text: This example telescopes a factorial series with a small but clever rewrite of the numerator.
The trick is to split the numerator. Write r as r plus one, minus one — a harmless-looking move that unlocks everything.
Now r over r-plus-one-factorial becomes r plus one minus one, over r-plus-one-factorial, which separates into one over r-factorial minus one over r-plus-one-factorial.
And that is exactly a difference of consecutive reciprocal factorials — a telescoper in disguise.
Summing, all the interior terms cancel, leaving one over one-factorial minus one over n-plus-one-factorial, which is one minus one over n-plus-one-factorial.
As n grows, the trailing factorial term races to zero, so the infinite sum is exactly one.

<curious> The habit worth carrying: for factorial sums, look for a way to write the term as f of r minus f of r plus one, where f is some factorial expression. Once you spot it, the collapse is automatic.

segments_hinglish.text: यह example एक factorial series को telescope करता है, numerator के एक छोटे पर clever rewrite के साथ।
trick है numerator को split करना। r को r plus one, minus one लिखो — एक harmless दिखने वाला move जो सब कुछ unlock कर देता है।
अब r over r-plus-one-factorial बन जाता है r plus one minus one, over r-plus-one-factorial, जो separate होता है one over r-factorial minus one over r-plus-one-factorial में।
और यह exactly consecutive reciprocal factorials का एक difference है — disguise में एक telescoper।
sum करने पर, सारे interior terms cancel हो जाते हैं, बचता है one over one-factorial minus one over n-plus-one-factorial, यानी one minus one over n-plus-one-factorial।
जैसे-जैसे n बढ़ता है, आख़िरी factorial term zero की ओर दौड़ता है, तो infinite sum exactly one है।
<curious> ले जाने लायक habit: factorial sums के लिए, term को f of r minus f of r plus one लिखने का तरीका ढूँढो, जहाँ f कोई factorial expression हो। जैसे ही spot करो, collapse automatic है।

82.title: A surd telescoper, evaluated at n = 99

board_content.text: Sum Σ 1/(√r + √(r+1)), then evaluate for n = 99
Rationalise the denominator to unlock the difference-form.
Rationalising turns a sum of awkward fractions into a clean telescoper.

segments_english.text: This Advanced example telescopes a surd series, and the key move is rationalising the denominator.
Each term looks intimidating — one over root r plus root r plus one — but rationalising tames it completely.
Multiply top and bottom by root r plus one minus root r. The denominator becomes a difference of squares: root r plus one squared minus root r squared, which is just one.
So each term collapses to simply root r plus one minus root r — a clean consecutive difference.
Summing telescopes it: everything cancels except the endpoints, leaving root n plus one minus one.
Now evaluate at n equals ninety-nine: root of one hundred minus one, which is ten minus one, equal to nine.
<excited> That is the whole payoff — rationalising converted a sum of awkward-looking fractions into a clean telescoper, and a hundred-term sum came down to a single, tidy nine.

segments_hinglish.text: यह Advanced example एक surd series को telescope करता है, और key move है denominator को rationalise करना।
हर term डरावना दिखता है — one over root r plus root r plus one — पर rationalising इसे पूरी तरह वश में कर लेता है।
ऊपर-नीचे को root r plus one minus root r से multiply करो। denominator बन जाता है difference of squares: root r plus one squared minus root r squared, यानी बस one।
तो हर term बस root r plus one minus root r में collapse होता है — एक clean consecutive difference।
sum करने पर यह telescope होता है: endpoints के अलावा सब cancel, बचता है root n plus one minus one।
अब n equals ninety-nine पर evaluate करो: root of one hundred minus one, यानी ten minus one, बराबर nine।
<excited> यही पूरा payoff है — rationalising ने awkward दिखने वाली fractions के sum को एक clean telescoper में बदल दिया, और सौ-term का sum एक अकेले, tidy nine पर आ गया।

83.title: Telescoping: the traps and the pro-tips

board_content.text: Telescoping — the traps, and the fast moves
No difference-form: brute-forcing or applying $\sum n^k$ to a fraction/surd.
Endpoint sign: the answer is $V_1 - V_{n+1}$, not $V_0 - V_n$ — watch off-by-one.
Lost multiplier: keep the $\tfrac12$ or $\tfrac1k$ the split carries.
$V_n$ divisor: divide by (number of factors + 1).
Pro-tip: fraction → partial fractions; product → $V_n$; surd → rationalise.
Factorials → write $t_r = f(r+1) - f(r)$.
After telescoping, the answer is always (first survivor) − (last survivor).

segments_english.text: Let's close Unit eight with the telescoping traps and the fast moves that beat them.
The dominant error is failing to reach a difference-form at all — brute-forcing the sum, or trying to apply the polynomial standard-sum formulas to a fraction or a surd, where they simply don't fit.
Second is the endpoint sign. After collapse, the answer is V-one minus V-n-plus-one — not V-nought minus V-n. Off-by-one on the surviving endpoints is the main slip.
Third, don't lose the multiplier. When the split carries a one half or a one over k, that constant must ride all the way through to the final answer.
Fourth, in the V-n method, divide by the number of factors plus one — the wrong divisor quietly wrecks the result.

<curious> Now the decision tree. For a fraction, try partial fractions and look for a consecutive-shift difference. For a product of consecutive terms, use the V-n method. For a surd in the denominator, rationalise.
And for factorials, hunt for a way to write the term as f of r plus one minus f of r, with f a factorial expression.
Above all, remember the shape of every telescoping answer: it is always the first surviving term minus the last surviving term. If your answer isn't in that form, you haven't finished collapsing.

dominant error है difference-form तक पहुँच ही न पाना — sum को brute-force करना, या एक fraction या surd पर polynomial standard-sum formulas apply करने की कोशिश करना, जहाँ वे fit ही नहीं होते।

तीसरा, multiplier मत खोओ। जब split एक one half या one over k रखे, वो constant final answer तक पूरे रास्ते साथ चलना चाहिए।
चौथा, V-n method में, number of factors plus one से divide करो — गलत divisor चुपके से result बर्बाद कर देता है।

<curious> अब decision tree। एक fraction के लिए, partial fractions try करो और एक consecutive-shift difference ढूँढो। consecutive terms के product के लिए, V-n method use करो। denominator में surd के लिए, rationalise करो।
और factorials के लिए, term को f of r plus one minus f of r लिखने का तरीका ढूँढो, f एक factorial expression के साथ।
सबसे ऊपर, हर telescoping answer का shape याद रखो: यह हमेशा first surviving term minus last surviving term है। अगर तुम्हारा answer उस form में नहीं, तो तुमने collapse पूरा नहीं किया।
